instructions: In a bowl, whisk the flour, sweet rice flour, baking soda, baking powder, sugar and salt.

In another bowl, whisk the egg with 3/4 cup of water and 1 tsp of the oil. Pour it into the dry mix and whisk until the batter is thin, like crepe batter. Transfer it to a pitcher or measuring cup with a spout.
Heat a fish shaped bungeoppang or taiyaki pan, closed, over medium heat for about 1 minute on each side. Lower the heat to medium-low and brush every mold with a little of the 1 tbsp oil.
Fill each mold about a third full with batter. Add about 2 teaspoons of red bean paste to the center of each and pour in more batter to fill the mold.
Close the pan and flip it. Cook for 2 to 2 1/2 minutes, flip, and cook for 2 to 2 1/2 minutes, until they're golden brown and crisp.
Transfer the pastries to a rack and repeat with the rest of the batter, oiling the molds each time.
Let them cool for a few minutes before the first bite. The red bean paste stays very hot.
method_notes: Sources agree on a thin batter poured into a fish shaped pan with red bean paste in the middle. The lead uses milk and an optional butter on the pan; water and oil are used here so it stays dairy-free, which a second source lists as an option. Batter is scaled up by a third to make about 8 pastries. You need a bungeoppang or taiyaki pan. Both sources were read, but neither has enough ratings to lead, so this is a fallback.
